data.name: Jabbaar
data.gender_notes: Jabbaar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'J-B-R', meaning 'to shake, to make things move'. In Islamic context, Jabbaar refers to Allah (swt) as The Thunderer or The Mighty One. The name symbolizes strength, power, and divinity. The name Jabbaar carries the meaning “The Thunderer, The Mighty One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jabbaar usually hope their child will grow to embody the thunderer, the mighty one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A leader or protector who brings people or resources together
data.etymology: Jabbaar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Thunderer, The Mighty One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jabbaar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: جبار
in_arabic.meaning: القوي الذي له القدرة على كل شيء
in_arabic.long_meaning: جبار هو اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني القوي الذي له القدرة على كل شيء، وهو الذي يجبر الخواطر ويسلط على كل شيء بقدرته. ورد اسم الله الجبار في القرآن الكريم في عدة آيات، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَهُوَ الْجَبَّارُ الْعَزِيزُ' (سورة ص: 68). ويستخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية كاسم لله تعالى، ويعبر عن قوته وجبروته.

in_urdu.name: جبار
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ تعالیٰ کا نام، مضبوط اور قادر
in_urdu.long_meaning: جبار اللہ تعالیٰ کے ناموں میں سے ایک ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مضبوط اور قادر۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں بھی ذکر کیا گیا ہے، جیسے کہ سورہ ص میں: 'وَهُوَ الْجَبَّارُ الْعَزِيزُ' (سورة ص: 68)। مسلم ثقافت میں، یہ نام اللہ تعالیٰ کی طاقت اور قدرت کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: जब्बार
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान का नाम, मजबूत और समर्थ
in_hindi.long_meaning: जब्बार भगवान के नामों में से एक है, जिसका अर्थ है मजबूत और समर्थ। यह नाम कुरआन में भी आया है, जैसे कि सूरा साद में: 'وَهُوَ الْجَبَّارُ الْعَزِيزُ' (सूरा साद: 68)। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम भगवान की शक्ति और सामर्थ्य का प्रतीक है।

in_pashto.name: جبار
in_pashto.long_meaning: جبار د الله تعالیٰ له نومونو څخه يو دی، چې مانا يې د ځواکمن او پياوړی دی. دا نوم په قرآن کريم کې هم راغلی دی، لکه څنګه چې د سورت ص آيت 68 کې: 'وَهُوَ الْجَبَّارُ الْعَزِيزُ'۔ په افغان او پښتون دود کې، دا نوم د الله تعالیٰ د قدرت او پياوړتیا نښه ده.

in_english.name: Jabbaar
in_english.meaning: Powerful and mighty, one of Allah's names
in_english.long_meaning: Jabbaar is one of the names of Allah, meaning powerful and mighty. This name is derived from the Arabic root 'ج-ب-ر' which implies strength and power. The name Jabbaar is mentioned in the Quran, for example, in Surah Sad: 'وَهُوَ الْجَبَّارُ الْعَزِيزُ' (Surah Sad: 68). In Islamic tradition, Jabbaar signifies Allah's omnipotence and authority. The name is used across Muslim cultures to invoke the attributes of strength and might associated with Allah.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jabbaar in Arabic culture holds a revered status particularly in the context of prophetic stories. In Islamic tradition, Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham, peace be upon him) is believed to have been scared of a mighty thunder storm, which caused him distress. Allah (swt), in response to Prophet Ibrahim's fear, revealed His Ability to control the elements and demonstrated this power with a thunderbolt, reassuring Prophet Ibrahim and making him realize Allah's Omnipotence. This event is commemorated in some cultures, like Algerian, with specific customs and practices, under the name 'Ressas' or 'Thunderstorm Festival'.
data.spiritual_significance: Jabbaar, as a name for Allah (swt), signifies Allah's absolute power, dominion, and control over everything in existence. It highlights Allah's ability to create jaw-dropping phenomena like thunderstorms, and the responsiveness of all of creation to His command. In the Quran, Allah is described as the One with 'Power over all things' (37: 3-4). The name Jabbaar reminds Muslims of Allah's immense might and glory that transcends all boundaries and serves as a reminder to have full faith in Allah's power, even during times of adversity.
